cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Profession – A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification.

p.em: Example: Jim sings an upbeat 80s R&B song warning young people against choosing law as a profession.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disillusionment – A feeling of disappointment resulting from the discovery that something is not as good as believed.

p.em: Example: Many law graduates experience deep disillusionment when faced with endless paperwork and billing hours.

cosy-blockquote.p: Burnout – State of emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged stress.

p.em: Example: Working 80-hour weeks at a corporate firm is a guaranteed recipe for career burnout.

cosy-blockquote.p: Litigation – The process of taking legal action in court.

p.em: Example: Corporate litigation often involves reviewing thousands of dry documents rather than dramatic court arguments.

cosy-blockquote.p: Billable – Capable of being billed to a client, especially for professional services.

p.em: Example: Lawyers live under constant pressure to record as many billable hours as possible each day.

cosy-blockquote.p: Alternative – Available as another possibility or choice.

p.em: Example: The song humorously suggests almost any alternative career is better than practicing law.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prestige – Widespread respect and admiration felt for someone on the basis of their achievements or quality.

p.em: Example: People choose legal careers for societal prestige, but prestige does not guarantee happiness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Debt – A sum of money that is owed or due.

p.em: Example: Taking on huge student debt for law school forces graduates to take corporate jobs they dislike.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fulfillment – Satisfaction or happiness as a result of fully developing one's abilities or character.

p.em: Example: Finding personal fulfillment in your job is far more valuable than a impressive job title.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sabbatical – A period of paid or unpaid leave granted for study, travel, or rest.

p.em: Example: Jim took a permanent sabbatical from law to run a local broom shop instead.

ul.li: Incorrect: Don't be a lawyer for get rich → Correct: Don't become a lawyer to get rich ((Use 'to + infinitive' for purpose.))
Incorrect: He is tired from his job → Correct: He is tired of his job / exhausted from his job ((Use 'tired of' for boredom/dissatisfaction.))
Incorrect: She works as lawyer → Correct: She works as a lawyer ((Include indefinite article 'a' with professions.))
